name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the ancient Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital in Dimapur, featuring distinctive mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and carved monoliths dating to the 10th-13th centuries.
facts: Ancient capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom before Ahom invasion.
Features mushroom-shaped pillars carved with birds, animals and motifs.
Maintained by Archaeological Survey of India.
Located behind Naga Shopping Arcade in Dimapur town.
Best visited October to March.

name: Diezephe Craft Village
description: Handicraft village renowned for traditional Naga woodcarving, bamboo and cane work, and loinloom weaving, with artisan workshops, museum and Weaver’s Place homestay.
facts: Home to skilled weavers and craftsmen of Tenyimei/Chakhesang communities.
Promoted by Nagaland Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation.
Hosts annual International Loinloom Festival in early December.
About 13 km from Dimapur; now primarily in Chümoukedima district.
Recognized as Best Tourism Village 2023.

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex featuring a stone sculpture garden with works by Indian artists, traditional morungs, amphitheatre and Northeast Heritage Museum.
facts: Showcases 31 stone sculptures by artists from across India.
Houses North East Heritage Museum with crafts from eight NE states.
Located near Dimapur Airport, about 3 km from railway station.
Includes children’s park and hanging bridge.
Open for cultural programmes and public visits.

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped family park within the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, Dimapur, offering boating, ziplining, water zorbing, kids train and picnic spots amid greenery.
facts: Located inside State Horticulture Nursery grounds.
Features adventure activities and restaurant.
Nominal entry fee; popular for picnics.
Best time October to March.
Easily accessible from Dimapur city centre.

name: Nagaland Zoological Park
description: State’s main zoo at Rangapahar spanning 176 hectares, housing native Northeast Indian fauna including hornbills, hoolock gibbon, tigers and other species; part of Rangapahar Wildlife Sanctuary.
facts: Opened in 2008; closed on Mondays.
Focuses on Northeast Indian biodiversity with ~40 species.
Located about 6-8 km from Dimapur; now in Chümoukedima district.
Entry fee applies; ideal for families.
Adjacent to Rangapahar Reserve Forest for birdwatching.

name: Triple Falls (Seithekima)
description: Scenic three-tier waterfall near Seithekima village cascading about 280 feet into natural pools, surrounded by lush forest; popular for picnics, photography and light trekking.
facts: Three distinct streams forming a natural spectacle.
About 18-26 km from central Dimapur.
Managed with tourism support; best post-monsoon.
Approach involves short trek through greenery.
Note: area associated with Chümoukedima district.

name: Dimapur Town
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland on the Dhansiri River plains, serving as the primary entry point with airport, railway station and bustling markets reflecting Naga and multi-ethnic culture.
facts: Only major plains city in hilly Nagaland.
Key rail and air hub for the state.
Historic Kachari capital area.
Vibrant markets including Hong Kong Market for handicrafts and goods.
Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors from outside Nagaland.

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for imported and local goods, clothing, electronics, and Naga handicrafts; a lively commercial hub popular with locals and tourists.
facts: One of Dimapur’s most famous markets.
Sells traditional Naga garments, bamboo crafts and everyday items.
Central location near major transport points.
Best explored during daytime.
